posts.hook: Week 1 vs Week 12 on the same 5-day plan.
posts.caption:
Nobody "got lucky" here. This is 12 weeks of the Gym Fat Loss Protocol — Prime, Strip, Polish. Same 5 sessions a week, protein held at 1g per lb, a controlled deficit, and two refeed weeks so you don't crash. The result isn't a secret. It's a structure.

posts.hook: Why your cut stalls at week 5 (and how a refeed fixes it).
posts.caption:
Slide 1: The stall is metabolic, not moral.
Slide 2: 4+ weeks in a deficit and your body defends its weight — leptin drops, NEAT quietly falls.
Slide 3: A planned refeed week at maintenance carbs resets hormones and refills muscle glycogen.
Slide 4: That's why the Fat Loss Protocol builds TWO refeeds into 12 weeks — Strip and Polish phases.

Structure beats willpower. Full plan, free — link in bio.
posts.notes: Carousel = authority format. Teaches a real mechanism, ties to real phase names.

posts.hook: You're not bulking. You're just getting fat.
posts.caption:
A +10% surplus adds muscle. A +40% surplus adds a belly and a longer cut later. The Gym Mass Builder targets 0.5–1 lb per week on purpose, re-baselined every 4 weeks. Slow is the fast way.

The whole Lean Bulk plan is free. Link in bio.

posts.hook: No gym. No equipment. Still no excuse.
posts.caption:
The Home Fat Loss Starter is 4 short bodyweight sessions a week — squats, push-ups, inverted rows off a table, reverse lunges. Plate-based portions, no food scale for the first month. Month 3 looks nothing like month 1 because the progression is built in.

Start at home. Link in bio.
posts.notes: Removes the #1 objection (no gym). Paid $10 bundle.

posts.hook: Protein per pound, by goal — the only cheat sheet you need.
posts.caption:
Cutting hard? 1.2–1.3g/lb.
Recomp? 1.1g/lb.
Lean bulk? 1.0g/lb.
Beginner / maintenance? 0.8–0.9g/lb.

Higher protein on a cut isn't bro-science — it's how you keep muscle while the scale drops. Every TJFit bundle sets the target for you. Swipe for the full breakdown.
posts.notes: Saveable reference post — high share/save rate. Pulls real targets from bundles.ts.

posts.hook: Lifting heavy didn't make her bulky. It made her strong.
posts.caption:
Glute-focused lower days, balanced upper work, macros tuned to a woman's training week. The Women's Strength & Sculpt program puts strength first — the shape is the result, not the goal. Hip thrusts, Bulgarians, RDLs, and a plan that respects your cycle.

Strong is the whole point. Link in bio.

posts.hook: 6 lifts. 3 days a week. That's the whole beginner game.
posts.caption:
You don't need 12 exercises and a supplement stack. Beginner Foundations is goblet squat, DB bench, DB row, RDL, plank, walk — 3 days a week, linear progression, no food weighing. Learn, apply, confirm. Twelve weeks and you'll have real strength and a habit that sticks.

Start from day one. Link in bio.
posts.notes: Beginner is the biggest addressable audience.

posts.hook: Strength training after 50 isn't risky. Losing muscle is.
posts.caption: The Lifelong Strength Protocol is built around joints, not against them — leg press over back squat, chest-supported rows, mobility woven into every session, protein spread across 4 meals. Three days a week. It's never too late to get stronger; it's only ever too early to quit.
posts.notes: Underserved audience, high trust value. Static works for older demo on IG.

TJAI is the coach built into TJFit: it knows your program, adjusts your plan, and talks you through the hard weeks — in 5 languages. Not a chatbot bolted on. A coach that follows the thread.

Meet your coach. Link in bio.
